title: Width 512 -> 640 at depth 12 (ASPECT_RATIO 40 -> 48)
description: One constant: ASPECT_RATIO 40 -> 48, so model_dim 512 -> 640 with 5 heads of 128 at unchanged depth 12; nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE / wash: val_bpb 0.986885 vs baseline 0.986277, i.e. 0.0006 worse, inside the ~0.0009 noise floor. Numbers: params 71.3M -> 100.9M, FLOPs/token 3.46e8 -> 5.03e8 (+45%), total_tokens 331.5M -> 245.6M (-26%), num_steps 2529 -> 1874, steady-state MFU 38.5% -> 41.4%, peak VRAM 32.1 -> 40.7 GB. So +45% capacity-per-token bought back exactly the 26% of tokens it cost and nothing more. Read together with depth (8->10 -0.0082, 10->12 -0.0027), this says we have reached the compute-optimal frontier for this 5-minute budget: both capacity directions now trade ~1:1 against tokens, and the model shape (12 layers, dim 512, 4 heads of 128) is approximately right rather than accidentally narrow -- my 'aspect ratio 42.7 is anomalously thin' argument was wrong, or at least not binding. Do not buy depth 14 or dim 768; the remaining 16 runs should go to knobs that change quality per FLOP without changing size: MLP expansion ratio (4x is untested), WINDOW_PATTERN, and WARMDOWN_RATIO / schedule shape, which is the only major constant block nobody has touched all cell.
